title: Butter Tarts
subtitle: flaky shells filled with brown sugar, butter and a runny caramel centre, raisins optional
imageAlt: Canadian butter tarts with glossy caramel filling and raisins on a white plate, one bitten to show a runny centre

beforeYouStart.text: Bake on the lowest rack so the bottoms of the shells crisp.
Keep the shells frozen until they're filled: cold pastry stays flakier.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F) with a rack in the lowest position. Set the frozen tart shells on a rimmed baking sheet and scatter the raisins into them, if using.

steps.title: Mix the filling
steps.text: Whisk the brown sugar, corn syrup, melted butter, egg, vanilla, vinegar and salt just until smooth. Don't whisk in air or it will foam up in the oven.

steps.title: Fill
steps.text: Fill each shell about two-thirds full. Any fuller and it bubbles over.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 15–18 minutes, until the pastry is golden and the filling is puffed and bubbling across the whole surface. The centres will still jiggle slightly.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Cool 10 minutes on the sheet, then lift onto a rack. The filling sets as it cools; a runny centre is the Canadian way.

fixIt.fix: Fill only two-thirds full and always bake on a rimmed sheet.
They came out too soon. Bake until the filling bubbles all over, not just at the edges.
Use the lowest rack, and put the shells in straight from the freezer.
Don't skip the vinegar, and don't overbake.

saleTip: Tenderflake and store-brand frozen tart shells are often 2 for $7 at No Frills in December.
swap: Currants instead of raisins are the old-fashioned choice. Maple syrup can replace half the corn syrup for a maple butter tart; the filling sets a little softer.
leftovers: Warm one for 5 minutes in the oven and serve with vanilla ice cream.
doneness: The filling is puffed and bubbling across the whole surface, not just at the edges. That's when the egg is cooked. The centres may still jiggle.
source: Based on classic Canadian butter tart methods (Canadian Living, Tenderflake): brown sugar, corn syrup, butter, egg and a little vinegar, baked in deep tart shells on the bottom rack.
prepAhead: Mix the filling up to 2 days ahead and keep it in the fridge; whisk before filling.
Bake and freeze: they thaw in about 30 minutes.
reheat: Serve at room temperature (20 minutes out of the fridge), or warm 5 minutes at 180°C (350°F).

basic.note: The plain filling: no raisins, no vanilla.

fancy.note: Pecan butter tarts with softly whipped cream.

stepNotes.0: Fancy: scatter the chopped pecans into the shells instead of raisins.

addSteps.title: Whip the cream
addSteps.text: Whip the cream with the icing sugar to soft peaks and spoon a little beside each tart.

plating: Serve slightly warm so the centre runs.
A spoon of whipped cream on the side, not on top.
Two per plate, one cut open.

why.0-7: A teaspoon of vinegar keeps the sugar from crystallizing, so the filling stays smooth and gooey.
why.0-3: Golden corn syrup gives the classic runny centre.

funFact: Butter tarts are one of the few truly Canadian desserts. The earliest printed recipe is in the Royal Victoria Hospital cookbook from Barrie, Ontario, in 1900, and raisins-or-no-raisins is still a national argument.

keeps.note: cool completely, freeze on a tray, then bag
keeps.thaw: On the counter about 30 minutes, or warm 5 minutes at 180°C (350°F)
